Haydon Hall, 110 Laurier Avenue West, Ottawa, on Wednesday, September 9, 2026 beginning at 10:00 a.m. The Mayor, Mark Sutcliffe, presided over the meeting from Council Chambers with some Members attending in person and the remaining Members participating remotely by Zoom.

Demolition Control – 344 McRae Avenue
Post-Flood Residential Resilience Support

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS the July 1, 2026 extreme rainfall event caused significant flooding impacts across the City of Ottawa, including in Ward 7 and the Crystal Beach community; and
WHEREAS flooding may occur through a variety of pathways, including overland flow, sewer surcharge, groundwater infiltration, and private-side plumbing or drainage limitations; and
WHEREAS the most appropriate flood-mitigation measures vary from property to property depending on how flooding occurred and the characteristics of the home; and
WHEREAS residents may experience challenges identifying the appropriate expertise, services, and information required to assess flooding impacts and evaluate potential mitigation measures; and
WHEREAS Council has previously provided direction regarding flood-event response, flood-resilience review activities, fee relief measures, and the City's Compassionate Grant Program and Residential Protective Plumbing Program; and
WHEREAS Council would benefit from information regarding potential approaches to supporting residents in navigating property assessment and flood-mitigation decision-making;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Council direct the General Manager, Infrastructure and Water Services, in consultation with relevant departments, to report back through the 2026 Rainfall Analysis on options to develop a private-property flood resilience toolkit that complements existing Council directions;
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff engage relevant stakeholders and service providers to identify existing supports, and potential partnership opportunities; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff examine how existing residential flood-resilience programs and initiatives, including Rain Ready Ottawa and related homeowner-support measures could contribute to improving resident access to information, guidance, and support following flooding events; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff undertake a jurisdictional review of homeowner-support, technical-assistance and private-side flood-mitigation programs offered by comparable Canadian municipalities and assess their applicability to Ottawa.

sub_agendas_items.title: Anti-Human Trafficking Task Force Framework

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS human trafficking is a serious crime and violation of human rights that disproportionately affects women, girls, youth, Indigenous peoples, newcomers, members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community, and other vulnerable populations; and
WHEREAS Statistics Canada data indicates that 416 police-reported human trafficking incidents were recorded in the Ottawa Census Metropolitan Area between 2014 and 2024, representing approximately 8.2 per cent of all police-reported incidents in Canada during that period, with Ottawa experiencing a rate significantly higher than the national average; and
WHEREAS the Ottawa Police Service Human Trafficking Unit reviewed 266 reports for possible human trafficking between January 1, 2023, and July 24, 2026, resulting in numerous criminal charges, demonstrating the continued prevalence of trafficking in Ottawa; and
WHEREAS Ontario's Anti-Human Trafficking Strategy 2025-2030 identifies prevention, early intervention, survivor supports, Indigenous-led approaches and enhanced coordination among partners as key priorities and includes a provincial investment of more than $345 million to combat human trafficking; and
WHEREAS numerous organizations in Ottawa currently provide critical services, supports, prevention programs, victim assistance, law enforcement, health, housing, education and community-based interventions related to human trafficking; and
WHEREAS there is an opportunity for the City of Ottawa to strengthen coordination, identify system gaps, improve information sharing, enhance prevention efforts and develop measurable community-wide objectives without duplicating the work of existing service providers and agencies;
WHEREAS in 2026, City Council approved Ottawa's refreshed2021 to 2031 Community Safety and Well-Being (CSWB) Plan, with a priority on gender based violence and violence against women. The plan sets out how the City works with community partners to improve the safety, health and well-being of Ottawa residents;
WHEREAS the as part of the CSWB Plan, the City has funded local community agencies to develop a community-led three-year Gender-based and Intimate Partner Violence Reduction Action plan (GBV-VAW Action Plan), informed by extensive sector engagement.
WHEREAS  A New Day Youth and Adult Services, and other Ottawa-based organizations contribute outstanding efforts to supporting survivors of human trafficking and sexual exploitation through trauma-informed care, long-term housing, counselling, and individualized recovery programs.
WHEREAS through its survivor-centered approach, A New Day empowers young people to heal, rebuild their lives, and move toward independence with dignity, hope, and community support.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Community and Social Services (CSSD) work with A New Day, and other organizations contributing to a GBV-VAW Action Plan, under the CSWB Plan, to create a Human Trafficking Task Force as a multi-sector, survivor-informed advisory body with the objective of improving community coordination, prevention, accountability and system-level responses to human trafficking in Ottawa to be announced in Q4 of 2026; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Task Force shall not duplicate the operational mandates of existing service providers, law enforcement agencies, community tables, or provincial programs, but shall instead focus on strategic coordination, policy advice, systems planning, advocacy to all levels of government and public education and awareness; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the appointed Task Force will develop the final structure, terms of reference, membership composition and governance model for the Task Force.

agenda_items.title: Motions Requiring Suspension of the Rules of Procedure

sub_agendas_items.title: Eastern Bridge Project

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following Motion to engage the federal government in a timely manner prior to the anticipated end of the consultation period.
WHEREAS Public Services and Procurement Canada’s proposed Eastern Bridge Project includes not only a new interprovincial crossing but modifications to approximately nine kilometres of existing roads, intersections and multi-use pathways along the Montée-Paiement - Aviation Parkway corridor, extending from Autoroute 50 in Gatineau to Highway 417 in Ottawa; and
WHEREAS the project could have significant implications for traffic, truck movements, public transit, commute times, neighbourhood safety and Ottawa’s broader transportation network, including the intersections with Hemlock Road, Montreal Road, Ogilvie Road, Highway 174 and Highway 417; and
WHEREAS decades of discussion about an additional interprovincial crossing have generated deeply held and often opposing views across Ottawa, contributing to consultation fatigue without achieving a broadly supported regional transportation solution; and
WHEREAS the movement of people and goods is a regional issue that requires a coordinated approach and should not result in communities being pitted against one another based on where traffic impacts may be experienced; and
WHEREAS the Eastern Bridge Project must be understood within the context of the National Capital Region’s broader and long-term transportation needs, including traffic, truck movements, public transit, existing infrastructure and alternative regional routes and connections; and
WHEREAS Council has previously supported comprehensive, data-driven consideration of alternative regional transportation routes and a coordinated regional transportation planning framework, and any further work should build upon existing studies and Council directions rather than duplicate them; and
WHEREAS the National Capital Commission’s Long-Term Integrated Interprovincial Crossings Plan provides a “One Region” framework for the movement of people and goods across the National Capital Region; and
WHEREAS the current consultation concerns the Initial Project Description and represents an early step in a multi-stage impact-assessment and approval process; and
WHEREAS the current federal consultation period closes on October 9, 2026, during Ottawa’s municipal election period, limiting the ability of Members of Council to communicate and engage fully through municipal channels and concluding before the newly elected City Council takes office; and
WHEREAS a project requiring significant public investment warrants meaningful municipal and public participation before consequential decisions are made.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that City Council request that the Government of Canada extend the current consultation period and pause consequential decisions or approvals concerning the Eastern Bridge Project until the newly elected Ottawa City Council has taken office and had a reasonable opportunity to consider the matter and establish a formal City position; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that City staff engage with Public Services and Procurement Canada, the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada, the National Capital Commission and municipal, provincial and transit partners across the National Capital Region to support a coordinated discussion about the movement of people and goods and ensure that the proposed bridge is considered within the region’s broader and long-term transportation needs; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that these discussions build upon existing studies, available transportation data and previous Council directions, including consideration of public transit and regional routes and connections, to avoid duplication and ensure that the work remains relevant to Ottawa’s transportation planning regardless of whether the Eastern Bridge Project proceeds; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the extended consultation provide affected communities with a meaningful opportunity to understand and comment on the potential impacts and benefits; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the City Clerk formally submit this resolution through the federal impact-assessment process before the October 9, 2026 deadline, and that staff from Planning, Development and Building Services engage directly with the relevant federal agencies to advance Council’s requests, and provide Council with an update on the federal response and recommended next steps; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that this motion is not interpreted as Council’s final support for or opposition to the Eastern Bridge Project, but as a request for sufficient time, information and regional coordination before consequential decisions are made.

sub_agendas_items.title: Trump Avenue Street Name Change

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS the Central Park neighbourhood in Ottawa’s River Ward, was built in the late 1990s and early 2000s; and
WHEREAS many of the streets in Central Park were named after New York City landmarks, locations and an individual; and
WHEREAS one of the streets in the neighbourhood is named Trump Avenue, after Donald J. Trump, a New York City real estate mogul at the time of the naming and current President of the United States of America; and
WHEREAS the Central Park street naming theme was not proposed as a commemorative naming initiative and simply thematically named; and
WHEREAS Trump Avenue today would not meet any of the criteria had it gone through a formal commemorative naming process; and
WHEREAS City of Ottawa prides itself on who it commemorates and honours; and
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa's street naming policies require all new and replacement street names to be evaluated against established street naming criteria, including public safety and wayfinding considerations, to ensure that proposed names do not duplicate, sound the same as, or create confusion with existing or reserved street names and to support effective emergency response, navigation, and municipal addressing functions.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that City Council approve the renaming of Trump Avenue; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that City Council direct the Councillor for Ward 16, River Ward, to lead a public consultation process with all households of Trump Avenue that will ultimately nominate a new street name that meets the City’s street naming policies, which may retain a New York City theme or propose a name that deviates from that theme; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the proposed new street name be recommended to City Council for approval no later than Q2 of 2027.

sub_agendas_items.title: Municipal Support for a National Plan to Reduce and End Homelessness
Ottawa Community Housing Corporation Temporary Financing for Capital Repairs

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS Ottawa Community Housing Corporation (OCHC) is the City of Ottawa's wholly-owned municipal housing corporation, which manages approximately two-thirds of the social housing stock under the administration of the City, and provides housing to approximately 32,000 residents; and WHEREAS on October 8, 2025 through report ACS2025-CSS-GEN-012, Council approved the refinancing of five Public Housing properties between 2026 and 2028, expected to generate approximately $133 million for urgent and critical capital repairs within the OCHC portfolio; and
WHEREAS the timing of capital repair expenditures may not align with the receipt of mortgage refinancing proceeds, or other long-term financing sources, creating a need for interim financing to advance necessary repair work; and
WHEREAS the City has access to short-term financing instruments at rates that could be lower than the borrowing rates OCHC would have access to; and
WHEREAS short-term financing to OCHC is permitted and consistent with section 107 of the Municipal Act, 2001, provided that Council determines the financing to be in the interests of the City; and
WHEREAS the provision of temporary financing to OCHC for capital repairs supports the Term of Council Priority for the preservation and maintenance of affordable and social housing assets owned by OCHC, and assists the City in fulfilling its obligations as Service Manager under the Housing Services Act, 2011 and is therefore considered to be in the interest of the City;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Council approve the provision of temporary short-term financing by the City of Ottawa to Ottawa Community Housing Corporation, through the issuance of Promissory Notes or other short-term borrowing instruments, to finance capital repairs within the OCHC housing portfolio pending the receipt of mortgage refinancing proceeds, CMHC funding, or other long-term financing sources; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that all principal and interest associated with such temporary financing shall be repaid to the City by OCHC from operating revenues, or other available OCHC funding sources, such that the temporary financing does not result in an additional financial burden to City taxpayers; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Chief Financial Officer/Treasurer be delegated the authority to negotiate, execute, and administer all necessary agreements, Promissory Notes, repayment agreements, and related documents required to implement such temporary financing.

sub_agendas_items.title: City of Ottawa contribution to Canadian Red Cross appeal for July 2026 flood-impacted residents

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS more than 6,500 Ottawa households continue to cope with the significant emotional, physical, and financial impacts of flooding to their homes arising from the July 1, 2026 extreme weather and flood event; and
WHEREAS the Canadian Red Cross has been assisting hundreds of residents and families in need since July 1, helping them meet basic needs, access supports, navigate complex insurance claims and restore their homes; and
WHEREAS the Canadian Red Cross has now gained a greater understanding of the extent of the financial hardship that hundreds of uninsured and underinsured residents are facing and will continue to face in the coming months and years; and
WHEREAS the Government of Canada announced on September 4, 2026 that it was establishing a donation matching program in response to the Canadian Red Cross donation appeal campaign for flood-impacted residents in Ottawa, in order to maximize donations and help our residents in need get back on their feet;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that City Council institute a similar mechanism to match all donations from Canadian individuals and corporations made through the Canadian Red Cross appeal campaign, applied retroactively to the launch day of the appeal campaign on July 15, and up until the federal 90-day matching period ending on October 15; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED the City’s total contribution to the donation campaign up to $250,000, to be funded from the Tax Stabilization Reserve; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Canadian Red Cross report back to the City no later than Q2 2027 on how the funding helped flood-impacted residents in need.
